schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The Form, embodied — the base-most layer of the whole spine, composing no one and composed by everyone. Seven files under one charter: (1) core_values.py — the frozen CP1-CP6 contract (`CoreValue`, `CORE_VALUES`, `CoreValuesMixin`); (2) device.py — `BaseDevice`, which composes the mixin and declares the Form v0 #2 introspection surface (intention -> state -> settings -> other, assembled in order by concrete `introspect()`); (3) shim.py — `BaseShim`, which composes the mixin, pins `device_id`, and carries the per-pulse PROBE-FIRING: on each ground_loop heartbeat pulse, a device's shim evaluates its device's probes (each trigger where its data is owned, Law 6) and POKES the target of every one that fires, onto the bus — it also receives the device's mail and STARTS the device (its own process) on demand; (4) probe.py — the `Probe` primitive: an immutable 'poke X when this trigger is true', where a trigger is ANY predicate (not a named kind), the anti-reification made structural. Because both bases mix in `CoreValuesMixin`, every device and every shim carries the six structurally — you cannot be a device or a shim without them; and because probe-firing lives in the shim base, 'hang your probes on the heartbeat' is built into every device by inheritance, not re-implemented per device. The Form v0 #2 surface now has its first RENDER-side consumer built into the base pair (web-server ticket, child a): `BaseDevice.declared_panes()` lets a device OFFER extra panes beyond the STATUS+SETTINGS floor (each a handler returning DATA), and `BaseShim.active_page()` is the standard assembly — it projects the floor from `introspect()`, appends the declared panes in order (multiples of a kind allowed), renders an unwired or raising handler ABSENT-with-reason (CP2/Law 7), and returns pure DATA the web server renders. The machinery lives once in the base (Law 6), not per device. (5) diagnostic.py — `DiagnosticBase`, composed by `BaseDevice` so every device inherits `emit()` the way it inherits CP1-CP6: the transition-grade diagnostic surface Cairn lacked (outcome-grade VALIDATIONs/journeys said what PASSED; nothing spoke when system_rackmount went red SILENTLY). At a gate contact a device sends a THIN breadcrumb home to CC's shim (the diagnostic mailbox, for now — `BaseShim.receive_diagnostic`/`diagnostics()`), pointing to the ticket (`pointer`, the tie) and stamped to the microsecond (which indexes the fuller 30-day cache-class logs). The gate issues it — not the ticket; the emission stays dumb so the interpreter that crawls it can be smart (Law 1). Only the µs-stamp idea is carried from UU's `DiagnosticBase`; the loguru/JSON-sink backend is not. (6) transitions.py — the EMIT-CHOKEPOINT, the RULES rung of the state-transition trichotomy (state-machine-physics.json / harbor-master.json): the one door a workflow's cursor moves through. It parses the versioned workflow string (`code-seam@v1: THINKME -> ... -> [CURSOR] -> ... -> PROVED`), validates a requested transition against the class DEFINITION's machine-readable `workflow_versions` table (node_classes/<class>.json) + the -ME grammar (a summons ends -ME; forward advances or skips only declared-skippable summonses like TICKETME; a back-edge re-enters any earlier summons, carrying severity), REFUSES the illegal (a skip past a gate, an off-vocabulary target, an unknown class/version, a no-op, a path that does not conform to the version it claims), and journals the legal crossing append-only through the projector door (the charter-split's write-door — the TRUTH rung mechanism). It turns /sorted's prose 'refuses illegal transitions' into physics (Law 4). AUTHORITY (who may) is NOT here and never will be — that is the harbor_master's clearance gate (harbor-master child b); base owns the rules + the recording mechanism. CORRECTED 2026-08-10 (ticket emit-refuses-an-uncleared-crossing), and the superseded words are kept because they were the load-bearing falsehood: this read 'which WRAPS THIS CALL', which invited the reading that every emit caller necessarily passed through clearance. It never did — measured, 0 of 186 emit-shaped records on disk had ever carried cleared_by. What is true since 2026-08-10 is narrower and is physics: clearance is a SIXTH SEAT AT THIS SAME DOOR, a sibling of the five gates already inside emit, and it fires on a FORWARD JOURNALED CROSSING INTO A REST — the move that enters proven-space. Such a crossing carries the harbor's witness (cleared_by + the proof and seal it leaned on) or is refused before anything is written (ClearanceRequiredRed), and base RE-READS the Law 8 half of that witness against the world rather than trusting it. Base still asks WHO MAY nothing: it verifies only that the authority rung RAN, which is a Law 7 record-completeness question, and it imports nothing from harbor_master — not even an exception type. (7) nest.py — the block-general BAND VOCABULARY, ASSEMBLY and SHAKE (ruling 2026-08-07-the-nest-is-block-general, ticket banding-berths-at-the-general-level): `BAND_NAMES` (data — a tenant may extend it), `nest(reaches)` — bands assembled coarsest-first, empty bands omitted — and `shake(assembled, subjects, fire)` — the tenant brings the firing closure; the general side owns the coarse-first ordering, the binary gradation ({subject: {sieve: 0.0|1.0}} — a sieve that did not fire is ABSENT, never a third value) and the min() roll-up (never mean — one zero sinks the subject; an empty shake scores 1.0). Berthed HERE because a band's MEANING is block-general and a consumer of the gradation (the sieve-learning nexus is the named candidate) must read it at a general address, not inside one tenant; DERIVATION of a band — reach_of and the ladder — stays with import_sieve, because how a band is computed for an import-shaped sieve is that deriver's own craft. build_inspector rides this berth as tenant #1; the watch that keeps the generality honest is probes/does_the_gradation_find_a_reader.py. (8) address.py — BASE OWNS THE INSTANCE-SPACE ADDRESS, AND THAT OWNERSHIP STOPS AT RESOLUTION. Added 2026-08-12 (ticket one-owner-for-the-instance-address). The three roots {repo, commons, instance} and the four-rung ladder Akien ruled that day — TOOLS -> MACHINES -> DEVICES -> DEVICE INSTANCES, laid out as devices/<device>/<instance>/ with tools/<name>/ and machines/<name>/ beneath, ADDRESSED BY NAME NEVER BY ORDINAL — live here as resolve() plus instance_path/tool_path/machine_path. The root table was born in cairn/machines/skill_block/counters.py and was lowered here because base could not stand on a table at a device's address; counters re-exports it, so a charter author's rooted token (instance/devices/chart/0/packets) and a caller's device+instance arguments are TWO FACES OF ONE TABLE, pinned to each other by Path equality in proofs/test_instance_address.py. CLASS-SPACE ADDRESSING RESOLVES BOTH WAYS since 2026-08-14: ``component_dir`` takes a NAME to a home (raising on a name two rungs answer to, because neither home is an answer), and ``component_of`` takes a PATH to the component that owns it, returning the DEEPEST ancestor — components nest, so a file under a device's machine sits under both, and the shallower one is the holder rather than the address. The second half was added because constrain's floor was testing path-shaped refs for membership in a set of NAMES and silently discarding 86% of them; a caller holding the wrong shape should reach for the lookup that takes it, never guess. THE EDGE IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: this module COMPUTES addresses and NEVER PROVISIONS — no mkdir, no create-on-read — because a module that knows every device's address and also creates would be a Law 6 crossing written once and called convenient; instance space belongs to the device that owns it, and provisioning is a different act with a different owner. It also takes NO POSITION on whether a name is a device: membership is ground_loop/discovery's and the predicate is deviceness.py's, and a path resolver that quietly became the roster would be a second answer to a settled question. WHAT REFUSES A FURTHER HAND-SPELLED PATH, since 2026-08-17 (ticket the-instance-address-is-resolved-never-spelled). This paragraph used to read "nothing REFUSES an eleventh hand-spelled path ... the enforcement is a tracked debt", and those words are quoted here rather than deleted because they were the load-bearing truth for five days and because the two sites it named as legitimately-unconverted BOTH turned out not to be. address_rule.py is now the ONE spelling of the rule — an AST predicate over an EXPRESSION rather than a text scan, so a MENTION of the address in prose (an ast.Constant) can no longer be confused with a SPELLING of it (an ast.BinOp), and no file needs excluding by name. It is shaken at two moments and only ever authored once: build_inspector's address_is_resolved_never_spelled sieve REDS THE BUILD at inspection, and probes/hand_spelled_instance_paths.py reports on a pulse. The corpus measures 0 sites over 274 files, with an exemption set that is a RULE WITH TWO MEMBERS rather than a list of names — the module that owns the address, and any file under a proofs/ directory — bearing weight at the PROVED crossing in three files (address.py:94, aider_shim/proofs/test_fence.py:285, inference_domain/proofs/test_route.py:128 and :130). Three files, two members: the count of files rises whenever a proof asserts the rule and says nothing about the rule widening, which is exactly the distinction the ticket's wrong-intent clause turns on — a member that cannot be stated as "a file whose job is to name or to assert the rule" would mean this had become the hand-widened allowlist that reachability-replaces-the-allowlist retired at this same address. THE TWO NAMED HOLD-OUTS ARE CONVERTED AND THE REASONS ARE WHY THIS IS PHYSICS NOW: inference_domain/route.py was called a standing disagreement between two rulings, and moved (hosts.json now berths at devices/inference_domain/0/, byte-identical); build_inspector/inspector.py was called a rung the ladder does not have, and resolve("instance/devices") was that rung all along — its stated line number (:216) had drifted to :224 while nobody looked, which is what a named floor costs. RESIDUE, and it is the rule's own declared blind spot, not a gap in the enforcement: a path built by string concatenation from a variable, by a dynamic join, by an f-string, or through an aliased pathlib is invisible to an AST rule that reads Path.home() as a bare name. A stronger rule is a real improvement and is not this ticket's.
why: Law 2 — CP1-CP6 hold everywhere, including in the process that builds the system. A value enforced by prose is policy; a value carried by a class you cannot subclass without is physics (Law 4). NARROWED 2026-08-11 (ticket device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim), superseded words kept because they were the load-bearing falsehood: that sentence used to do double duty, standing as the argument for CP1-CP6 AND as this component's claim to DEFINE what a device is. Only the first half survives. Akien ruled the axis on 2026-08-11 — 'a shim fits TO the device; you + your shim = your device', and 'the unit is the FOLDER, not the registration: a device is a directory with a probes/ subdirectory, its id the directory's own name' — and Calibre was a device with no device code at all, just its shim, so no class read can ever admit that member. MEASURED the same day: 12 components are devices under the ruling and 11 of them subclass BaseDevice not at all, while 8 subclass it and are not on the roster the beat reads (bus and ground_loop among them); exactly one, librarian, is on both. WHAT THIS COMPONENT NOW POINTS AT INSTEAD OF ASSERTING: the predicate is cairn/tools/base/deviceness.py (is_device / fitted_device_ids / divergence), composing cairn/devices/ground_loop/discovery.py, which owns membership; the divergence is watched by cairn/tools/base/probes/device_claims_match_shims.py. THE NARROWING TOUCHES THE CLAIM ONLY, never the physics: BaseDevice stays subclassable and keeps composing CoreValuesMixin and DiagnosticBase, and introspect() keeps its ordering — falsifier clauses (3), (4) and (5) below are unchanged and three live component charters are red on them. Form v0 #2 lives here for the same reason: a uniform introspection surface on the base means every device is observable by construction, not by each device remembering to be — the tester probes one protocol, the web UI renders one protocol. That surface is the component's REAL why and it is the SAME axis Akien named; inheritance was its delivery mechanism, not its value, which is why the ruling costs this charter a claim and not a class. Placing the values here is necessary but not sufficient: a value is *consumed* only when a per-device contract turns it into a check (CP1 -> no 'done' without an honesty gate). This layer guarantees structural presence and the shape of the introspection surface; consumption is per-device charter work.

feedback.why: THE RULES RUNG REPORTS TO THE AUTHORITY RUNG, AND THE CALLER IS REAL RATHER THAN DESIGNED: cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py:84 imports emit from this module — measured, and independently visible in orient's census, which had to disambiguate harbor_master's transitions.emit call from its own device surface. transitions.py names the split itself: RULES here, AUTHORITY at the harbor_master's clearance gate. Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. What comes in as this door's input is a CROSSING somebody asked for, and the party that asks is the clearance gate. So a refused transition — an illegal move for that class@version, a malformed workflow string, a WATCHME with no probe — is feedback the clearance gate can act on, by refusing earlier or by clearing differently. It is also the address that most needs to hear it: clearance is RULED MANDATORY (ruled 2026-08-10) and measured NOT YET WRAPPING this door (186 emit-shaped records, zero carrying cleared_by), so this route points at the rung whose absence is the standing debt.

invoke: import: `from cairn.tools.base.core_values import CoreValuesMixin, CORE_VALUES`; `from cairn.tools.base.device import BaseDevice`; `from cairn.tools.base.shim import BaseShim`; `from cairn.tools.base.probe import Probe`; `from cairn.tools.base.diagnostic import DiagnosticBase`; `from cairn.tools.base import transitions`; `from cairn.tools.base.nest import BAND_NAMES, nest, shake`; `from cairn.tools.base.address import instance_path`. MEASURE THE PROBE-FEEDBACK RULE END TO END: `cairn probescan` (bin/cmd/probescan; `--json` for data, `--mail` for the traffic triage alone). It belongs to THIS charter because both ends of the contract it measures are declared here — `Probe` is the send end and `BaseShim.deliver` is the receive end — and the scan walks the same path the postman walks rather than reading for a `def receive`, which would be the structural proxy this corpus keeps catching in its own instruments. It reaches the ground_loop's roster only as the means of finding the devices; the rule it judges is base's. It is an INSTRUMENT run by a hand, not a standing watch: a probe watching all probes is the manager smell, and the scan deliberately does not arm itself (`scan()` is importable for a watch that later wants it). Exit 0 = every probe's feedback path whole end to end. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_core_values.py`, `test_composition.py`, `test_probe.py`, `test_shim.py`, `test_diagnostic.py`, `test_transitions.py`, `test_nest.py` (each exit 0 = green).

falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) the code and the canonical commons record (`CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/core-values.md`) disagree on the set, order, or any narrative (per that record's own falsifier); (2) `CORE_VALUES` is not exactly [CP1..CP6] in order, or the frozen `CoreValue` becomes mutable; (3) `BaseDevice` or `BaseShim` stops composing `CoreValuesMixin`, or any imported subclass of them overrides `CORE_VALUES` to a divergent set; (4) `introspect()` stops reporting intention -> state -> settings in that order; (5) `BaseDevice` stops composing `DiagnosticBase` or `emit` stops being inherited (a device that cannot send diagnostics home breaks 'transition-grade surface everywhere'), or a homeless `emit` silently DROPS a record instead of holding it loud (Law 7 — the silent-red defect this exists to end); (6) the emit-chokepoint (transitions.py) ADMITS an illegal transition — a forward skip past a gate summons, an off-vocabulary target, an unknown class/version, a no-op self-loop, or a path that does not conform to the version it claims — instead of refusing it loudly (that would make the state vocabulary policy again, not physics — Law 4/7), OR journals a crossing anywhere but append-only through the projector door (Law 7). (7) THE PROOF RECORD, ruled 2026-08-13 ("EVERYTHING ALWAYS PROVED AND LISTING WHAT IT PROVED. SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE"): a journaled crossing carrying no `proved` list, or a `checks_proved` counted beside the list rather than derived from it — the gate and its own sentence drifting apart; (8) a lane whose `expected` and `actual` cannot be `==` when it PASSES — the authoring hazard measured n=4 across the corpus in one day, which reds every HEALTHY subject; both sides read the same sentence when the lane passes and the offending value rides in `values`. Its only physics is proofs/test_transitions.py::test_a_healthy_subject_produces_an_all_passing_record_at_every_inspector, which runs every inspector at this door on a fixture known to be well; (9) a gate note or a findings list built BESIDE the record rather than RENDERED FROM it — derived, never parallel; two mouths for one question is how a gate and the sentence it prints come to disagree; (10) a lane whose input the lane above it refused appearing in the record as a PASSING entry rather than being ABSENT — a check that did not run is absent, not passed, and one fault must yield exactly one failing entry; (11) the proof roster in proofs/ being HAND-TYPED — a tooth nobody listed is a tooth that did not run and the file prints the same green line, which is this same defect one level up (caught twice by hand on 2026-08-13 before it was made physics); (12) `bin/cmd/determinism` ceasing to list cairn/tools/base as a PURE DETERMINISTIC GATE — this door holds gates, so it may never reach an oracle.
how_it_learns: The values themselves do not learn autonomously — by design. They are a frozen, ratified contract (Law 2), the terminal floor the rest of the system stands on; nothing-is-terminal does not apply to the axioms themselves. Their horizon is human: the words change only when Akien re-ratifies them (see core-values.md horizon). The Form v0 surface *does* have a learning path, but not here: each device charter answers, for itself, which CP became which enforced check and whether that check earns its keep, and the report *shape* firms up from what its consumers (tester, web UI) actually need. The base only guarantees the six are present to be consumed and the introspection surface is ordered and uniform.
